skill.name: pnpm
skill.description: Node.js package manager with strict dependency resolution. Use when running pnpm specific commands, configuring workspaces via pnpm-workspace.yaml, or managing dependencies with catalogs, patches, overrides, config dependencies, or the global virtual store.
skill.summary: Guide pnpm commands, workspace configuration, dependency policies, patches, CI workflows, migrations, performance, and supply-chain controls.
skill.author: antfu

security_audit.summary: The audit found no prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent. Most static alerts are Markdown syntax, example paths, placeholders, or safe configuration guidance. Confirmed concerns include credential-file inspection, recursive permission changes, third-party registry use, blanket build approval, unpinned execution, and destructive cleanup.

remediation.issue: The primary instructions encourage checking .npmrc, which can contain live registry credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Prohibit reading or displaying .npmrc values unless the user explicitly requests authentication troubleshooting. Require redaction of every token and certificate value.

remediation.issue: The supply-chain guide presents blanket dependency build approval without a direct warning.
remediation.suggestion: Remove blanket approval guidance. Require users to inspect and approve each dependency build script individually.

remediation.issue: The migration guide executes an unpinned codemod through pnpx.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed codemod version and verify its provenance before execution. Request confirmation before downloading or running it.

remediation.issue: The permission fix applies recursive chmod to a dynamically resolved path.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve and display the store path first. Reject root, home, and unexpected paths, then request confirmation before changing permissions.

remediation.issue: Migration and rollback examples delete project files without a backup or confirmation step.
remediation.suggestion: Create backups or rely on clean version control. Validate the working directory and request confirmation before every recursive deletion.

remediation.issue: The performance guide recommends a third-party package registry as the default.
remediation.suggestion: Use the official registry by default. Present mirrors only as opt-in choices with trust, privacy, and integrity warnings.

semantic_findings.title: Blanket Dependency Build Approval
semantic_findings.description: The guide lists blanket build approval without a nearby warning. This authorizes every pending dependency lifecycle script, allowing unreviewed package code to execute.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented command explicitly approves all pending builds. Dependency lifecycle scripts can execute arbitrary code with the installer account.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Codemod Execution
semantic_findings.description: The migration guide runs an unpinned codemod through pnpx. A compromised or malicious latest release could execute arbitrary code during migration.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command names no package version or integrity value. pnpx may download and execute the registry-selected release.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Cleanup Without Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The rollback example recursively deletes dependencies, the lockfile, and workspace configuration. It provides no backup, path validation, or confirmation step before deletion.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command directly names pnpm-workspace.yaml and uses recursive forced deletion. The surrounding rollback steps do not preserve or restore that configuration.

content.value_statement: Complex pnpm workspaces require precise commands and configuration. This skill provides focused guidance for dependencies, CI, migrations, patches, performance, and supply-chain controls.
actual_capabilities: Explains core pnpm install, add, remove, update, run, filter, publish, and runtime commands.
Guides workspace configuration for catalogs, overrides, peers, patches, and package-specific settings.
Provides CI examples for GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Docker, caching, and frozen lockfiles.
Supports migrations from npm, Yarn, Lerna, and pnpm version 10 configuration.
Explains content-addressable stores, virtual stores, node linkers, and performance settings.
Describes build approvals, release-age controls, trust policies, and lockfile integrity.
limitations: Guidance targets pnpm 10 and selected pnpm 11 changes; behavior may differ in later releases.
It does not inspect package provenance or verify registry, proxy, hook, patch, and dependency trust.
It cannot guarantee migration safety, command success, or compatibility with every workspace and operating system.
Publishing, cleanup, permission changes, credential access, and build approvals require explicit review before execution.

use_cases.title: Manage Application Dependencies
use_cases.description: Choose pnpm commands, dependency types, version policies, and verification steps for a Node.js application.

use_cases.title: Operate Monorepo Workspaces
use_cases.description: Configure workspace packages, catalogs, filters, shared settings, stores, and CI workflows across many projects.

use_cases.title: Migrate Package Management
use_cases.description: Plan a controlled migration from npm, Yarn, Lerna, or older pnpm configuration with rollback steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Dependency
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add [package] to [project]. Check its dependency type, then propose the pnpm command and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Workspace
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a pnpm workspace for [apps and packages]. Provide the layout, required settings, catalog strategy, and installation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review CI Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [CI configuration] for pnpm. Identify caching, version pinning, lockfile, script approval, and trust issues, then recommend precise changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Secure Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a migration from [current package manager] to [target]. Include backups, dependency validation, configuration changes, rollback steps, and security checks.

output_examples.input: Set up reliable pnpm CI for a monorepo.
output: Pins a compatible pnpm version and installs with a frozen lockfile.
Caches only the pnpm store across trusted jobs.
Builds changed packages with validated workspace filters.

output_examples.input: Migrate a Yarn workspace to pnpm.
output: Creates a staged migration plan with backups before file deletion.
Maps workspace packages and imports the existing lockfile.
Validates peer dependencies, scripts, builds, and rollback steps.
Reviews build scripts individually before approval.
Applies release-age, trust-policy, and lockfile-integrity controls.
Avoids untrusted registries and blanket security exceptions.

best_practices: Pin pnpm and use frozen lockfiles in CI.
Review dependency build scripts individually before approval.
Back up lockfiles and configuration before migrations or cleanup.
anti_patterns: Do not read, print, or expose registry tokens from .npmrc files.
Do not run recursive deletion or permission commands without validating paths and obtaining confirmation.
Do not use untrusted registries, unpinned executables, or blanket build approvals.

faq.question: Can this skill run pnpm commands?
faq.answer: It provides command guidance. The host agent controls execution and should request confirmation for destructive, publishing, or credential-related actions.

faq.question: Does it support pnpm 11?
faq.answer: It covers selected pnpm 11 changes, but primarily targets pnpm 10. Verify current documentation before adopting version-specific settings.

faq.question: Can it configure a monorepo?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains workspace packages, catalogs, filters, package-specific settings, shared stores, and CI patterns.

faq.question: Does it handle registry authentication?
faq.answer: It explains authentication file placement but should not read or display credential values. Use environment-backed secrets and redact outputs.

faq.question: Can it migrate npm or Yarn projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides migration steps, dependency checks, workspace conversion guidance, and rollback planning.

faq.question: Does it replace official pnpm documentation?
faq.answer: No. Use official documentation to verify current commands, defaults, compatibility, and security behavior before making significant changes.
